newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi dlr ends static, on hold for US payrolls data.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi dlr ends static, on hold for US payrolls data.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended Friday almost unchanged from its morning levels after staunchly holding its ground throughout the day amid apprehension of a possible drive by the Reserve Bank to tighten currently easy monetary conditions in the money markets, dealers said.

The bank said nothing, and conditions stayed easy, with the dollar's Trade Weighted Index (TWI) ending at 67.36, almost flat with its morning level of 67.37 and slightly easier than its 67.41 Thursday close.
The kiwi closed at 0.6865/73, just off its 0.6868/75 opening, and brokers said the whole market was waiting for a signal from key U.S. non-farm payrolls data due after the close from Washington.
"It's all open for Monday, really, and even the Reserve Bank will probably make up its mind depending on the non-farm payrolls (outcome)," a Wellington forex dealer said.

The currency was also underpinned by continuing Eurokiwi issuance, the latest being a NZ$100 million issue for the World Bank, and dealers said there was talk of another, larger issue soon. --Wellington newsroom +64 4 471 4273
